answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. zkSync account age proof flips the bet — an account active since the early days — and the plume lands on the attacker instead. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that an account active since the early days — so privacy survives, and the garden is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. Scale is the enemy of the attacker here. The nebula grows with every clone, but the reward per clone stays fixed, so the farm goes broke before it goes big.
